I wyll prayse thee O Lorde among the people: and I wyll sing psalmes vnto thee among the nations
For the greatnes of thy mercie reacheth vnto the heauens: and thy trueth vnto the cloudes
Exalt thy selfe O Lord aboue the heauens: let thy glory be aboue al the earth
O ye that consult together, pronounce ye truely the thing that is iust? O ye sonnes of men iudge you according to equitie
Nay, rather ye imagine mischiefe in your heart: your handes waygh as in a ballaunce wickednes vpon the earth
The vngodly are straungers euen from their mothers wombe: assoone as they be borne, they go astray and speake a lye
(58: 4a) They haue poyson [within them] lyke to the poyson of a serpent: they be lyke the deafe adder that stoppeth her eares
(58: 4b) and wyll not heare the voyce of charmers, though he be neuer so skilfull in charming
(58: 5) Breake their teeth O Lorde in their mouthes: smite a sunder the chawe bones of Lions O God
(58: 6) Let them be dissolued as into water, let them come to naught of them selues: and when they shoote their arrowes, let them be as broken
(58: 7) Let them creepe away lyke a snayle that foorthwith consumeth to naught: or lyke the vntimely fruite of a woman, let them not see the sunne
(58: 8) As a greene thorne [kindled with fyre, goeth out] before your pottes be made whot: euen so let a furious rage bring him to naught
(58: 9) The righteous wyll reioyce when he seeth the vengeaunce: he wyll washe his foote steppes in the blood of the vngodly
(58: 10) And euery man shall say, veryly there is a rewarde for the righteous: doubtlesse there is a God that iudgeth in the earth
Deliuer me from myne enemies O Lorde: defende me fro them that rise vp against me
Deliuer me from the workers of iniquitie: and saue me from the blood thirstie men
For lo, they lye in wayte for my soule: men of power are gathered together against me who haue committed no wickednes nor fault O God
When no fault is done, they runne and set them selues in order: arise to meete me and beholde
And thou O God Lorde of hoastes, Lorde of Israel: awake to visite all Heathen, and be not mercifull vnto all them that offend of malice. Selah
They go to and from at euening: they barke lyke a dogge, and runne about through the citie
Behold they speake with their mouth, swordes are in their lippes: for [say they] who doth heare [vs?
But thou O God wylt haue them in derision: thou wylt laugh all Heathen to scorne
I wyl reserue his strength for thee: for thou O Lorde art my refuge
My mercifull Lord wyll preuent me: the Lord will let me see [my desire] vpon mine enemies
Slay them not, lest my people forget it: but in thy stoutnes scatter them like vagaboundes, and put them downe O God our defence
The wordes of their lippes [be] the sinne of their mouth: O let them be taken in their pryde, for they speake nothing but curses and lies
Consume them in thy wrath, consume them that nothing of them remayne: and let them knowe that it is the Lord that ruleth in Iacob, & vnto the endes of the worlde. Selah
And let them gad vp and downe at euening: let them barke lyke a dogge, and go about the citie
Let them runne here and there for meate: and go to bed if they be not satisfied
As for me I wyll sing of thy power, and wyll prayse thy louing kindnes betimes in the morning: for thou hast ben my defence and refuge in the day of my trouble
Unto thee O my strength will I sing psalmes: for thou O Lorde art my refuge, and my mercyfull Lorde
O Lorde thou hast cast vs out, thou hast dispearsed vs, thou art displeased: O turne thee vnto vs agayne
Thou hast made the land to tremble, thou hast cleft it asunder: heale the breaches therof, for it is redy to fall downe
Thou hast made thy people see heauie thinges: thou hast geuen vs wyne to drinke, that maketh vs tremble
But to suche as feare thee: thou hast geuen a banner to be lyfted vp on high for the trueth sake. Selah
[ Therfore] that thy beloued may be deliuered: helpe me with thy right hand, and heare me
The Lorde hath spoken in his holynes (whereof I wyll reioyce) this: I wyll deuide Sichem, and measure the valley of Sucoth
Gilead shalbe myne, and Manasses shalbe myne: Ephraim also shalbe the strength of my head, and Iuda my law geuer
Moab shalbe my washpot: ouer Edom I wyll cast my shoe, Philistea be thou glad of me
Who wyll leade me into the stong citie? who wyll bring me into Edom
Hast not thou remoued vs from thence O Lorde? and wylt not thou O Lorde go out with our hoastes
Geue vs ayde against trouble: for the sauing helpe of man is but vayne
Thorowe the Lorde we wyll do valiaunt actes: for he him selfe wyll treade downe our enemies
Heare my crying O Lorde: geue eare vnto my prayer
From the endes of the earth I wyll call vnto thee when my heart is in heauines: oh set me vp on the rocke that is higher then I
For thou hast ben my hope: [and] a strong towre [for me] against the face of the enemie
I wyll dwell in thy tabernacle for euer: my trust shalbe vnder the couering of thy wynges. Selah
For thou O Lorde hast hearde my vowes: and hast geuen an heritage vnto those that feare thy name
Thou wilt adde dayes vnto the kings dayes: and his yeres shalbe a generation and a generation
He shall dwell before the Lorde for euer: O appoynt thy louing mercy and faithfulnes, that thei may preserue him
So wyll I sing psalmes vnto thy name: that I may day by day perfourme my vowes
My soule truly only stayeth vpon the Lorde: for of him commeth my saluation
He onlye is my rocke and my sauing helpe: he is my refuge, so that I can not be remoued greatly
Howe long wyll ye imagine mischiefe against euery man? ye shalbe slayne all the sort of you: [ye shalbe] as a tottering wall, [and like] a broken hedge
They deuise only howe to thrust [him] from his promotion: they delight in a lye, they blesse with their mouth, and curse with their heart. Selah
[ Neuerthelesse] O my soule, stay thou only vpon the Lorde: for my confidence is in him
He only is my rocke and my sauing helpe: he is my refuge, so that I can not be remoued
In the Lorde is my health and my glory: my trust is in the Lorde the fortresse of my force
O ye people, put your trust in hym alway: powre out your heartes before him, for the Lorde is our hope. Selah
As for the chyldren of men, they be onlye but vanitie, the chyldren of lordes be but a lye: vpon the wayghtes they [be] altogether [lighter] then vanitie in selfe
O trust not in wrong [dealing] and spoyling: geue not your selues vnto vanitie, if riches encrease, set not your heart [vpon them.
(62: 11a) The Lord spake it once, [but] I haue hearde it twise, that power and mercy belongeth to thee O Lorde God
(62: 11b) for thou rewardest euery man according to his worke
O Lorde thou art my Lorde: early in the morning I do seeke thee. (63: 2) My soule thirsteth for thee: my fleshe also longeth after thee in a baren and drye lande [where] no water is
(63: 3) [To see thee] euen so [as] I haue seene thee in the sanctuary: that I might beholde thy power and glory
(63: 4) For thy louing kindnes is better then life [itselfe ]: my lippes shall prayse thee
(63: 5) As long as I liue I wyll blesse thee on this maner: and in thy name I wyll lyft vp my handes
(63: 6) My soule is satisfied euen as it were with mary and fatnes: and my mouth prayseth thee with ioyfull lippes
(63: 7) Haue I not remembred thee in my bed: and thought vpon thee when I was waking
(63: 8) Because thou hast ben my helper: therfore vnder the shadowe of thy wynges do I reioyce
(63: 9) My soule cleaueth fast vnto thee: thy right hande hath vpholden me
(63: 10) And they [that] seeke my soule to oppresse [it ]: shall go vnder the earth
(63: 11) Euery one of them shalbe killed with the edge of a sworde: and they shalbe a portion for Foxes
(63: 12) But the king shal reioyce in the Lord, al they shal glory that sweare by him: for the mouth of all them that speake a lye, shalbe stopped
O Lorde heare my voyce in my prayer: preserue my life from feare of the enemie
Hyde me from the secrete [counsayles] of the malitious: from the conspiracie of the workers of iniquitie
Who haue whet their tongue lyke a sword: who haue drawne their arrow, euen a bitter worde
That they may priuily shoote at hym which is perfect: they do sodenly shoote at hym and feare not
They courage them selues in mischiefe: and comune among them selues how they may lay snares, and say, who shall see them
They searche out howe to do wrong, they put in practise fully that they haue diligently searched out: yea euen the secretes and bottome of euery one of their heartes
But the Lorde wyll sodenly shoote at them with a [swyft] arrowe: their plagues shalbe [apparaunt.
Yea they shall cause their owne tongues to be a meanes for to destroy the selues: insomuch that who so seeth them, shal desire to flee away [from them
And all men that see it shall say, this hath God done: for they shall well perceaue that it is his worke
The righteous wyll reioyce in God, and put his trust in hym: and all they that be vpright hearted wylbe glad
O Lorde thou wylt be greatly praysed in Sion: and vnto thee shal vowes be perfourme
Thou that hearest a prayer: vnto thee shall all fleshe come
[ My] misdeedes haue preuayled against me: oh be thou mercifull vnto our wicked transgressions
Blessed is the man [whom] thou choosest and receauest vnto thee: he shall dwell in thy court, and we shalbe satisfied with the goodnes of thy house, euen of thy holy temple
Thou wylt heare vs, doyng wonderfull thinges in righteousnes O Lorde of our saluation: thou [art] the hope of all endes of the earth, and of them that dwell farre of at the sea coast
Thou art he who in his strength setleth fast the mountaines: and is gyrded about with power
Who stilleth the raging of the sea, and the noyse of his waues: and the vprore of the people
They also that dwel in the vtmost partes [of the earth] be afrayde at thy signes: thou makest them reioyce at the going foorth of the morning and euenyng
Thou visitest the earth, and thou makest it ouerflowne, thou enrichest it greatly: the riuer of God is full of water, thou preparest their corne, for so thou ordaynest it
Thou waterest her forowes, thou breakest downe her hillockes: thou makest it soft with the drops of rayne, and blessest the increase of it
Thou crownest the yere with thy goodnes: and thy cloudes drop fatnes
They drop vpon the dwellinges of the wyldernesse: and hilles be compassed with ioy
The downes be couered with sheepe: the valleys stande thicke with corne [so that] they showte [for ioy] and also sing
(66: 1a) Declare you ioyfull vnto the Lorde all [ye of] the earth
(66: 1b) sing psalmes vnto the glory of his name, geue glory to his maiestie
(66: 2) Say vnto the Lorde, oh howe wonderfull art thou in thy workes: thorow the greatnes of thy power thyne enemies shalbe founde liers vnto thee
(66: 3) For all [they of] the worlde shall worship thee, and sing psalmes vnto thee: they shall sing psalmes vnto thy holy name. Selah
(66: 4) Come hither and beholde the workes of the Lorde: howe wonderfull he is in his doing towarde the chyldren of men
(66: 5) He turneth the sea into drye lande, so that they went thorowe the water on foote: there dyd we reioyce in him
(66: 6) He ruleth with his power for euer, his eyes beholdeth the gentiles: such as be rebels shal not come to promotion. Selah
(66: 7) O ye people blesse your Lorde: and make the voyce of his praise to be heard
(66: 8) Who preserueth our soule in life: and suffereth not our feete to slip
(66: 9) For thou O Lord hast proued vs: thou hast tryed vs, like as siluer is tryed
(66: 10) Thou broughtest vs into the snare: and layde trouble vpon our loynes
(66: 11) Thou sufferedst men to ride ouer our heades: we went through fire and water, and [yet] thou broughtest vs out into a pleasaunt [place.
(66: 12a) I wyll go into thy house with burnt offeringes: and I wyll pay thee my vowe
(66: 12b) whiche I promised with my lippes, and spake with my mouth when I was in trouble
(66: 13) I wyll offer vnto thee fat burnt sacrifices, with the incense of rammes: I will offer bullockes and goates. Selah
(66: 14) O come hither, & hearken: and I wil tell all you that feare the Lorde, what he hath done for my soule
(66: 15) I called vnto hym with my mouth: and I exalted him with my tongue
(66: 16a) If I had inclined vnto wickednes in my heart, the Lorde woulde not haue hearde me
(66: 16b) but the Lorde hath hearde me, & considered the voyce of my prayer
(66: 17) Blessed be the Lorde which hath not reiected my prayer: nor turned his mercye from me
The Lord be mercyfull vnto vs and blesse vs: [and] cause the light of his coutenaunce to shine vpon vs. Selah
That thy way may be knowen vpon the earth: thy saluation among all nations
[ Then] wyll the people prayse thee O Lorde: yea all the people wyll prayse thee
The Gentiles will reioyce & triumph: for thou wylt iudge the people, and gouerne the gentiles vpon the earth, according to equitie. Selah
The people will prayse thee O Lord: all the people wyll prayse thee
[ Then] shall the earth bryng foorth her increase: and the Lorde our Lord will geue vs his blessing
The Lorde will blesse vs: and all the endes of the worlde shall feare him
In case the Lorde woulde aryse, his enemies woulde be scattered: and they that hate hym woulde flee from his face
Lyke as the smoke vanisheth, [so] wylt thou cause [them] to vanishe away: and lyke as water melteth at the fire, [so] wyll the vngodly perishe at the presence of the Lorde
But the ryghteous must be glad, and reioyce before the Lorde: they shall not stande styll for myrth
Syng vnto the Lorde, syng psalmes vnto his name: magnifie hym that rideth vpon the heauens as it were vpon an horse in his name euerlastyng, and reioyce before his face
He is a father of the fatherlesse, and the iudge of widdowes: [he is] the Lord in his holy habitation
He is the Lord that maketh those that dwell alone to haue a familie: and bryngeth prisoners out of the stockes
But rebelles did inhabite a dry [ground] O Lorde, when thou wentest foorth before the people: when thou wentest through the wyldernesse. Selah
The earth shoke, and the heauens dropped at the presence of the Lorde: euen Sinai it selfe [shoke] at the presence of the Lorde, Lorde of Israel
Thou O Lorde dydst cause rayne to fall at thy gratious pleasure: and when thine inheritaunce was weery, thou dydst hearten it
Thy flocke dwelleth there: for thou O Lorde doest of thy goodnesse prepare for the poore
The Lorde gaue the worde: great was the company of the preachers
Kynges with their armies dyd flee: they dyd flee, and the ornament of an house deuided the spoyle
Though ye haue lyen among the pottes: yet shall ye be as the wynges of a doue that is couered with siluer, and hath her fethers as yelowe as golde
When the almightie scattered kynges in it: it was as whyte as snowe in Salmon
As the hyll of Basan, so is Gods hill: euen an hygh hyll, as the hyll of Basan
Why skyp you so the high hylles? this is the Lordes hyll in the which it pleaseth hym to dwell, yea God wyll abyde in it for euer
The charettes of the Lorde are twentie thousande, euen thousandes of angels: and the Lorde is among them in holy Sinai
Thou wenst vp on high, thou hast led captiuitie captiue, thou hast receaued gyftes for men: yea euen [for] those that be disobedient, that God the Lorde myght dwell [among them,
Blessed be the Lorde who day by day powreth his [benefites] vpon vs: and is God of our saluation. Selah
The Lorde is our Lorde for to saue vs: and all maner of wayes for death pertayneth to God the Lorde
God wyll wounde the head of his enemies: and the heary scalpe of hym who goeth on styll in his wickednesse
The Lorde hath sayde, I wyll bryng [my people] agayne out from Basan: I wyll bryng [them] agayne out from the deepe of the sea
That thy footes [and] the tongue of thy dogges: may be made redde in the blood of the enemies by his meanes
They do well see O Lorde thy goynges: thy goynges in the sanctuarie my Lorde and kyng
The singers go before, the minstrelles folowe after: in the myddest are the damselles playing with the timbrelles
In the congregations they do blesse the Lorde: the God of the fountayne of Israel
There is litle Beniamin their ruler, & the princes of Iehuda their counsell: the princes of Zabulon [and] the princes of Nepthali
Thy Lord hath ordeyned thy strength: establishe the thing O Lorde that thou hast wrought in vs
For thy temple sake at Hierusalem: kynges wyll bryng presentes vnto thee

Put to rebuke the companie of speare men, a multitude of bulles amongest the people lyke vnto calues: [vntyll] that they brought vnder foote [come] with peeces of siluer [for tribute,] scatter the people that delyght in warre
Then shal princes come out of Egypt: Ethiopia in all haste shall stretch out her handes vnto the Lorde
Sing vnto the Lord O ye kingdomes of the earth: O syng psalmes vnto the Lorde. Selah
Who rydeth vpon the most hyghest eternall heauens: lo he sendeth out a mightie voyce in his voyce
Acknowledge the Lorde to be mightie: his maiestie is ouer Israel, & might in the cloudes
O Lorde thou art terrible out of thy holy places: the God of Israel geueth myght and strength vnto his people, Blessed be the Lorde
Saue me O Lorde: for waters haue entred in vnto my soule
I am ouer the head in deepe myre where I feele no grounde: I plunge in deepe waters where the streame ouerwhelmeth me
I am weery of crying, my throte is drye: my syght fayleth me through the long attendaunce that I haue geuen vpon my Lorde
They that hate me without a cause are mo then the heeres of my head: they that are myne enemies and woulde destroy me giltlesse are mightie, I payde them the thynges that I neuer toke
God thou knowest my folly: and my faultes are not hyd from thee
Let not them that trust in thee O Lorde God of hoastes, be for my cause ashamed: let not those that seke thee, be through me confounded O Lorde of Israel
(69: 7a) For thy sake haue I suffered reprofe, shame hath couered my face
(69: 7b) I am become a straunger vnto my brethren, euen an aliaunt vnto my mothers children
(69: 8) For the zeale of thine house hath euen eaten me: and the rebukes of them that rebuked thee, are fallen vpon me
(69: 9) And I wept [chastenyng] my soule with fastyng: and that was turned to my reproofe
(69: 10) Also I put on sackcloth for my garment: and they iested at me
(69: 11) They that sit in the gate speake agaynst me: and they that drynke strong drynke [make] songes [vpon me.
(69: 12) But [I make] my prayer vnto thee O God in an acceptable tyme: heare me O Lord in the multitude of thy mercie, according to the trueth of thy saluation
(69: 13) Take me out of the myre, that I sincke not: oh let me be delyuered from them that hate me, & out of the deepe waters
(69: 14) Let not the water fludde drowne me, neither let the deepe swalowe me vp: & let not the pyt shut her mouth vpon me
(69: 15) Heare me O God, for thy louyng kindnesse is comfortable: turne thee vnto me accordyng vnto the multitude of thy mercies
(69: 16) And hyde not thy face from thy seruaunt, for I am in trouble: O haste thee [and] heare me
(69: 17) Draw nigh vnto my soule & redeeme it: for myne enemies sake oh redeeme me
(69: 18) Thou hast knowen my reproofe, my shame, and my dishonour: myne aduersaries are all in thy syght
(69: 19) Reproofe hath broke my heart a peeces, I am full of heauinesse: I loked for some to haue pitie on me, but there was none, and for some that shoulde comfort me, but I coulde fynde none
(69: 20) They gaue me for meate, gall to eate: and when I was thirstie, they gaue me vineger to drynke
(69: 21) Let their table be as a snare before them: and in steade of aboundaunce of peace, let it be a meanes of destruction
(69: 22) Let their eyes be blynded that they see not: and euer bowe downe their loynes
(69: 23) Powre out thine indignation vpon them: and let thy wrathfull displeasure take holde of them
(69: 24) Let their habitation be desolate: and let no man dwell in their tabernacles
(69: 25) For they persecute hym whom thou hast smitten: and they talke of the griefe of them whom thou hast wounded
(69: 26) Let them fall from one wickednesse to another: and let them not enter into thy ryghteousnesse
(69: 27) Let them be wyped out of the booke of the lyuyng: and not to be written among the ryghteous
(69: 28) As for me I am afflicted and in heauinesse: thy sauing helpe O Lorde shal defende me
(69: 29) I wyll prayse the name of the Lorde with a song: and magnifie hym with a solemne confession
(69: 30) And it wyll please God: better then a bullocke that hath hornes and hoofes
(69: 31) The humble wyll consider this and be glad, such as seke after God: and your soule shall lyue
(69: 32) For God heareth the poore: & dispiseth not his prisoners
(69: 33) Let heauen and earth prayse hym: the sea and all that moueth therin
(69: 34) For the Lorde wyll saue Sion, and builde the cities of Iehuda: that men may dwel there and haue it in possession
(69: 35) The posteritie also of his seruauntes shall inherite it: and they that loue his name shall dwell therin
Haste thee O Lorde to delyuer me: make haste to helpe me O God
Let them be ashamed and confounded that seke after my soule: let them be turned backwarde and be put to confusion that wishe me euyll
Let them be returned backwarde: for a rewarde of their shamyng [other] which say, there, there
But let all those that seke thee be ioyfull and glad in thee: and let all such as delight in thy saluation say alway, the Lorde be magnified
As for me I am poore and in miserie, hasten thee vnto me O Lorde: thou art my ayde and my delyuerer, O God make no long tarying
(71: 1a) In thee O God I haue put my trust, let me neuer be put to confusion
(71: 1b) ridde me and deliuer me in thy ryghteousnesse, incline thine eare vnto me, and saue me
(71: 2) Be thou my strong holde whervnto I may alway resort: thou hast geuen a charge to saue me, for thou art my house of defence, and my castell
(71: 3) Delyuer me O my Lorde out of the hande of the vngodly: out of the hande of the vnryghteous and cruell man
(71: 4) For thou O Lorde God art the thyng that I long for: thou art my hope euen from my youth
(71: 5) Through thee haue I ben mayntayned euer since I was borne: thou art he that toke me out of my mothers wombe, my praise shalbe alway of thee
(71: 6) I am become as it were a monster vnto many: but my sure trust is in thee
(71: 7) Oh let my mouth be fylled: with thy prayse and glorie all the day long
(71: 8) Cast me not away in the tyme of age: forsake me not when my strength fayleth me
(71: 9) For myne enemies speake against me: and they that lay awayte for my soule take their counsayle together
(71: 10) They say, the Lorde hath forsaken hym: do you persecute hym and take hym, for there is none to delyuer hym
(71: 11) Go not farre from me O Lorde: haste thee O my Lorde to helpe me
(71: 12) Let them be confounded, let them be brought to naught that are agaynst my soule: let them be couered with shame and dishonour that seke to do me euyll
(71: 13) As for me I wyll patiently wayte alway: and I wyll prayse thee more and more
(71: 14) My mouth shall dayly speake of thy ryghteousnesse and saluation: for I knowe no ende therof
(71: 15) I wyll go foorth in the strength of the Lorde God: [and] I wyll only make mention of thy ryghteousnesse
(71: 16) Thou O God hast taught me from my youth: and hytherto I can well declare thy wonderous workes
(71: 17) Wherfore whylest I am olde and am gray headed: O Lorde forsake me not, vntyll I haue shewed thy arme vnto [this] generation, and thy power to all them that are yet for to come
(71: 18) And vntyll I [haue] exceedyngly exalted O Lorde thy ryghteousnesse: for great thynges are they that thou hast done, O Lorde who is lyke vnto thee
(71: 19) Which hast made me to feele many great troubles and aduersities: yet returnyng thou hast reuyued me, yea returnyng thou hast caused me to come out from the bottome of the earth
(71: 20) Thou hast brought me to greater honour then I had before: & thou returnyng hast comforted me on euery syde
(71: 21) Therfore I wyll confesse vnto thee thy trueth O Lorde, playing vpon an instrument of musicke: vnto thee I wyl syng psalmes vpon the harpe O thou most holy [God] of Israel
(71: 22) My lyppes wyll be ioyfull when I syng vnto thee: and so wyll my soule which thou hast redeemed
(71: 23) My tongue also shal talke of thy righteousnesse all the day long: for they are confounded and brought vnto shame that seke to do me euyll
O God geue vnto the kyng thy iudgementes: and thy ryghteousnesse vnto the kynges sonne
[ Then] he wyll iudge thy people accordyng vnto iustice: and thy afflicted accordyng to equitie
The mountaynes also and hylles: shall bryng peace to the people by the meanes of ryghteousnesse
He wyll iudge the afflicted amongst the people: he wyll saue the children of the poore, and subdue the oppressour
They wyll feare thee as long as the sunne and moone shyneth: from one generation to another
He wyll come downe lyke the rayne into a fleece of wooll: euen as the droppes that water the earth
In his dayes the ryghteous wyll florishe: and there shalbe aboundaunce of peace so long as the moone endureth
His dominion also shalbe from the one sea to the other: and from the fludde vnto the ende of the earth
They that dwell in the wildernesse shal kneele before him: his enemies shal licke the dust
The kyng of Tharsis and of the Iles shall offer presentes: the kynges of Sheba & Seba shall bring giftes
All kynges wyll worshyp hym: all nations wyll do hym seruice
For he wyll delyuer the poore when he cryeth: and the afflicted and hym that hath no helper
He wyll haue compassion vpon the poore and needy: and he wyll preserue the soules of the poore
He wyll delyuer their soules from deceipt and oppression: and their blood shalbe in his syght
He wyll lyue, and he wyll geue to the poore of the golde of Sheba: and he wyll pray alwayes for hym, and dayly he wyll blesse hym
A handfull of corne shall [be sowed] in the earth vpon the toppe of hylles: and the fruite therof shall make a noyse lyke Libanus, and shall florishe in the citie lyke grasse vpon the earth
His name shall endure for euer, his name shalbe spread abrode to the world so long as the sunne shall shyne: all nations shalbe blessed in hym, and shall call hym blessed
Blessed be God the Lorde: the Lorde of Israel which only doth wonderous thynges
(72: 19a) And blessed be the name of his maiestie for euer: and all the earth shalbe fylled with his maiestie. Amen, Amen
(72: 19b) Here endeth the prayers of Dauid the sonne of Isai
Truely the Lorde is very good vnto Israel: vnto such as haue a cleane heart
Neuerthelesse, my feete were almost gone from me: my steppes had almost slypt
For I enuied at the case of the foolishe: I sawe the wicked [flowe] in all kynde of prosperitie
For there be no bondes of death that can holde them: and the galaries of their houses be strong
They come in no misfortune lyke other folke: neither are they plagued lyke other men
And this is the cause that pride compasse them rounde about: and crueltie couereth them as a garment
Their eyes stande out for fatnesse: and the cogitations of their heartes do passe from them
They make other dissolute, they speake oppression with iniurie: they talke proudely and presumptuously
For they stretch foorth their mouth vnto the heauen: and their tongue goeth through the worlde
Therfore [God] his people turneth thither: and there is drawen vnto them waters in a full [cuppe.
And they say, howe shoulde God perceaue it? is there knowledge in the most hyghest
Lo these vngodly and fortunate in the worlde: do possesse riches
Truely I haue cleansed my heart in vayne: and wasshed my handes in innocencie
All the day long I haue ben scourged: and chastened euery mornyng
If I shoulde say that I woulde iudge after this sort: lo then I shoulde condempne the generation of thy children
Therfore I considered howe I might vnderstande this: but it was to paynefull in myne eyes
Untyll I went vnto the sanctuarie of God: and vnderstood the ende of them
Truely thou doest set them in slippery places: and castest them downe headlong for to be destroyed
Oh howe be they brought to a destruction euen vpon a sodayne: they faynt, they consume away for very dread
They be as a dreame to a man after he is once waked: O Lorde thou wylt cause their image to be dispised in the citie
Ueryly thus was my heart inflamed: thus was my reynes pricked
So foolishe was I and voyde of vnderstanding: I was euen a bruite beast before thee
Neuerthelesse I am alway with thee: for thou hast holden me by my ryght hande
Thou hast guyde me with thy counsayle: and after that thou receauedst me with glorie
Whom haue I in heauen but thee? and there is none vpon earth that I desire besides thee
My fleshe and my heart fayleth: but God is the strength of my heart, and my portion for euer
For lo, they that kepe them selues a loofe from thee shall perishe: thou destroyest euery one that committeth fornication agaynst thee
But it is good for me to come neare vnto God: [wherfore] I put my trust in thee O Lorde God, that I may declare all thy workes
O Lorde wherfore dost thou forsake vs altogether? wherfore breaketh foorth thy anger agaynst the sheepe of thy pasture
Remember thy congregation, thou hast possest it nowe a long tyme: thou hast redeemed the rodde of thine inheritaunce, euen mount Sion wherein thou dwellest
Lyft vp thy feete for to destroy vtterly euery enemie: which hath done euyll in thy sanctuarie
Thyne aduersaries roare in the myddest of thy congregations: and set vp their banners for signes [of victorie.
He that hewed tymber afore out of thicke woddes [for to builde the temple:] was esteemed as one offeryng a present [to God] aboue
But nowe they breake downe into peeces all the carued worke therof: with axes and hammers
They haue set fire on thy holy places: they haue defiled the dwellyng place of thy name [castyng it downe] to the groud
Yea, they sayde in their heartes, let vs make hauocke of them altogether: thus haue they burnt vp all the houses of God in the lande
We see not our ensignes, there is not one prophete more: no not one is there amongst vs that vnderstandeth our case
O Lorde shall the aduersarie do this dishonour continually? shall the enemie blaspheme thy name for euer
Why withdrawest thou thy hande, yea thy right hande? consume [them, drawing] it out of thy bosome
Truely God is my kyng of olde: who worketh saluation in the myddest of the earth
Thou didst deuide the sea through thy power: thou brakest the heades of the dragons in the waters
Thou smotest the heades of Leuiathan in peeces: and gauest hym to be meate for the people in wildernesse
Thou broughtest out fountaynes and waters out of the harde rockes: thou dyddest drye vp mightie waters
The day is thine, & the nyght is thine: thou hast prepared the light & the sunne
Thou hast set all the borders of the earth: thou hast ordeyned summer and wynter
Remember this O God, the enemie hath dishonoured: and the foolishe people hath blasphemed thy name
O deliuer not the soule of thy turtle doue vnto a wylde beast: forget not the congregation of the poore for euer
Loke vpon the couenaunt: for darknesse of the earth hath replenisshed houses with iniquitie
O let not the simple go away ashamed: but let the afflicted & needy geue prayse vnto thy name
Arise O Lord, mayntayne thine owne cause: remember the dishonour that the foolishe man [doth] vnto thee dayly
Forget not the voyce of thine enemies: the mutteryng of them that hate thee ascendeth vp continually
We do confesse it vnto thee O lord, we do confesse it: for thy wonderous workes do declare thy name to be at hande
When I shall take tyme fyt for the purpose: I wyll iudge accordyng vnto ryght
The earth wasteth and all the inhabitours therof: I haue vpholded the pyllours of it. Selah
I sayd vnto fooles deale not so madly: & to the vngodly set not vp your horne
Set not vp your horne an high: [and] speake [not] with a stiffe necke
Because promotion commeth neither from the east nor from the west: nor yet from the south
For God is the iudge: it is he that putteth downe one, and setteth vp another
For in the hande of God there is a cup, and the wine is redde: it is full mixt, and he powreth out the same. (75: 9) But the vngodly of the earth do wring out: and drynke the dregges therof
(75: 10) As for me I wyll euer set foorth in wordes [the Lorde ]: I wyll sing psalmes to the God of Iacob
(75: 11) And I wyll breake all the hornes of the vngodly: but the hornes of the ryghteous shalbe exalted
In Iurie is God knowen: his name is great in Israel
At Shalem is his tabernacle: and his dwellyng in Sion
There he brake the arrowes of the bowe: the shielde, the sworde, and the battayle. Selah
Thou art honourable: and of more puissaunce then the mountaynes of robbers
The hygh couragious stomackes are spoyled, they haue slept their slepe: and the valiaunt souldiours coulde not finde their owne handes
At thy rebuke O God of Iacob: both the charet and horse be brought to naught
Thou, euen thou art dreadfull: and who may stande in thy syght when thou [begynnest] to be angry
Thou causest thy iudgement to be hearde from heauen: then the earth trembleth, and is styll
When God ariseth to iudgement: and to helpe all the afflicted vpon the earth. Selah
The fearcenesse of man shall turne to thy prayse: [and] the remnaunt of the fearcenesse thou wylt restrayne
Make vowes vnto God your Lorde, & perfourme them all ye that be rounde about hym: bryng presentes vnto hym that is dreadfull
He abateth the spirite of princes: he is dreadfull to the kynges of the earth
My voyce was vnto the Lorde, and I cryed: my voyce was vnto the Lord, and he hearkened vnto me
In the tyme of my trouble I sought the Lorde: my hande all the nyght catched & ceassed not, my soule refused comfort
I called to remembraunce God, and I was disquieted: I conferred with my selfe, and my spirite was wrapped in pensiuenesse. Selah
Thou dydst kepe the watche of mine eies: I was amased & coulde not speake
I dyd thynke vpon the dayes past: and on the yeres of the olde worlde
I called to remembraunce my psalme, song on the musicall instrument in the nyght tyme: I communed with myne owne heart, & searched out my spirites
What, wyll the Lorde forsake me for euer? wyll he be no more intreated to be fauourable
Is his mercie cleane gone for euer? and is his promise made from one generation to another, come vtterly to an ende
Hath God forgotten to be gratious? and will he shut vp his louing kindnesse in displeasure? Selah
And I sayde, this is my death: but the ryght hande of the most hyghest [may graunt] me yeres
I dyd call to remebraunce the workes of God almightie: for thy wonders done a great whyle a goe came into my mynde
I also gaue my selfe to muse of all thy workes: and I talked of all thy actes
Thy way O Lorde is in holynesse: who is so great a God as the Lorde
Thou art the God that doth wonders: thou hast made thy power knowen among the people
Thou hast redeemed thy people with a [mightie] arme: the sonnes of Iacob and Ioseph. Selah
The waters sawe thee O God, the waters sawe thee, they feared: yea the depthes of them moued out of their place
Thicke cloudes powred downe rayne, thinne cloudes gaue a noyse: and thine arrowes went abrode into al corners
The sounde of thy thunder was rounde about the [sky ]: the lightnynges shone through the worlde, the earth quaked and trembled
Thy way is in the sea, and thy pathes in the great waters: and thy footesteppes are not knowen
Thou dydst leade thy people lyke sheepe: by the hande of Moyses and Aaron
Heare my lawe O my people: enclyne your eares vnto the wordes of my mouth
I wyll open my mouth in a parable: I wyll declare harde sentences of the olde tyme past
Which we haue hearde and knowen: and such as our fathers haue tolde vs
We wyll not hyde them from their children: nay we wyll set foorth in wordes to the generation to come, the prayses of God, and his myght and wonderfull workes that he hath done
For he reuiued a statute in Iacob, and gaue Israel a lawe: in the whiche he commaunded our forefathers to teache their children
To the intent the posteritie shoulde knowe it, [and] children whiche shalbe borne: that they shoulde ryse vp and declare it to their children
That they shoulde put their trust in God, and not forget the workes of God: but kepe his commaundementes
And that they be not as their forefathers [were] a rebellious and a mutable generation: a generation that directed not their heart aright, and whose spirite cleaued not stedfastly vnto God
[ Like as] the children of Ephraim, which beyng harnessed & carying bowes: turned their backes in the day of battayle
They kept not the couenaunt of God: and they woulde not walke in his law
But they forgat his workes: and his wonders which he had shewed them
Marueylous thinges dyd he in the sight of their fathers: in the land of Egypt, in the fielde of Zoan
He deuided the sea and let them go thorowe: he made the waters to stande as on an heape
In the day time also he led them with a cloude: and all the night through with a light of fire
He cloued the harde rockes in the wildernes: & gaue them drinke therof, as it had ben out of the great deepe waters
He brought running streames out of a stonie rocke: and caused waters to gushe downe, like as out of riuers
Yet for all this they sinned still against hym: so that they prouoked the most hyghest in the wildernesse
And they temped god in their heartes: in requiring meate for their lust
They spake against God: they said, can God prepare a table in the wildernesse
Beholde, he hath smytten the stonie rocke, and waters haue gushed out, and streames haue flowed out aboundantly: but can he likewise geue bread, can he prouide fleshe for his people
Wherefore God hearde [them,] he was wroth, a fire was kindled in Iacob: and there arose vp heauy displeasure against Israel
Because they beleued not in the Lord: nor did put their trust in his saluation
And yet he commaunded the cloudes aboue: and opened the doores of heauen
He raigned downe Manna also vpon them, that they shoulde eate: and gaue them corne from heauen
[ So] man dyd eate the bread of angels: he sent them meate inough
He remoued the east winde from vnder the heauen: and through his power he brought in the south winde
He rained fleshe vpon them as thycke as dust: and fethered foules like as the sande of the sea
He let it fall among their tentes: euen rounde about their pauilions
So they dyd eate and were wel filled, for he gaue them their owne desire: neuerthelesse they were not alienated from their lust
But whyle the meate was yet in their mouthes, the heauy wrath of God came vpon them, and slue the welthyest of them: and made the chosen men of Israel to stoupe
For all this they sinned still: and beleued not his wonderous workes
Therfore their dayes dyd he consume in vanitie: & their yeres in a short [troublous] time
When he slue them, they sought hym: they repented them, and made God their morninges worke
And they remembred that the Lorde was their rocke: & that the Lorde most hyghest was their redeemer
Neuerthelesse they dyd but flatter him with their mouth: and they made hym a lye with their tongue
For their heart was not vpright with him: neither continued they faythfull in his couenaunt
Yet for all that he beyng most merciful: cleane pardoned all their misdeedes, and destroyed them not
Yea many a tyme he dyd much for to represse his anger: and neuer woulde suffer his whole rage to breake out
For he considered that they were but fleshe, and that they were euen a winde that passeth away & cometh not againe
How oft dyd they prouoke hym in the wildernes: & greeued hym in the desert
They turned backe and tempted the Lorde: and prescribed boundes to the most holy [God] of Israel
They thought not of his hande: in the day when he redeemed them from the enemie
Howe he had wrought his miracles in Egypt: and his wonders in the fielde of Zoan
For he turned into blood their riuers & fluddes: so that they might not drinke
He sent amongst them all kind of flyes who dyd eate them: and frogges who destroyed them
He gaue their fruites vnto the caterpiller: & their labour to the grashopper
He destroyed their vines with hayle stones: and their wilde figge trees with the harde frost
He smote their cattell also with haylestones: and their flockes with thunder boltes
He cast vpon them the rage of his furie, anger, disdayne, and trouble: by sending foorth euill angels amongst them
He made away to his indignation, & spared not their soule from death: he gaue their lyfe to be subiect to the pestilence
And he smote all the first borne of Egypt: the first fruites of concupiscence in the pauilions of Cham
But as for his owne people, he led them foorth like sheepe: and conducted them through the wildernesse like a flocke of cattell
He brought them out safely that they shoulde not feare: and ouerwhelmed their enemies with the sea
And brought them within the borders of his sanctuarie: euen to this mountayne which his right hand purchased
He dyd cast out the heathen also before them: he caused their land to be deuided among the for an heritage, & made the tribes of Israel to dwell in their tentes
Neuerthelesse, they tempted and displeased the most hyghest Lorde: & kept not his testimonies
They turned backewarde, and they went astray like their forefathers: they started aside like a bowe that breaketh
For they stirred hym to anger with their hygh places: and prouoked him to ielousie with their carued images
When the Lorde hearde this, he was wroth: & toke sore displeasure at Israel
So that he forsoke the tabernacle in Silo: the pauilion [wherin] he dwelt amongst men
He deliuered his force into captiuitie: and his glorie into the enemies hande
He gaue also his people ouer to the sword: and was wroth with his inheritaunce
Fire consumed his young men: and his maydens were not maryed
His priestes were slayne with the sworde: and his wydowes made no lamentation
But the Lorde awaked as though he had slept: like a giaunt making a triumphant noyse after wine
He smote his enemies in the hynder parts: & put them to a perpetual shame
He refused the tabernacle of Ioseph: and chose not the tribe of Ephraim
But he chose the tribe of Iuda: euen the hill of Sion which he loued
And there he buylded his temple on high: and layde the foundation of it like a grounde euer to continue
He chose also Dauid his seruaunt: and toke hym away from the sheepefoldes
As he was folowing the ewes great with young he toke hym: that he might feede Iacob his people, and Israel his inheritaunce
So he fed them according to the simplicitie of his heart: and guided them by the discretion of his handes
O Lord, the heathen are come into thyne inheritaunce: they haue defiled thy holy temple, they haue made Hierusale an heape [of stones
They haue geuen the dead bodies of thy seruauntes to be meate vnto the foules of the ayre: and the fleshe of thy saintes vnto the beastes of the lande
They haue shed their blood like water on euery syde of Hierusalem: and there is none to burie them
We are become an open shame vnto our neyghbours: a very scorne and derision vnto them that are rounde about vs
O God, howe long wylt thou be angry? shall thy ielousie burne lyke fire for euer
Powre out thine indignation vpon the Heathen that haue not knowen thee: and vpon the kingdomes that haue not called vpon thy name
For they haue deuoured Iacob: and layde waste his dwelling place
O remember not against vs sinnes that be past, with all speede let thy tender mercy preuent vs: for we are brought very lowe
Helpe vs O Lord of our saluation for the glory of thy name: deliuer vs, and be mercyfull vnto our sinnes for thy names sake
Wherefore do the Heathen say, where is nowe their God? let the vengeaunce of thy seruauntes blood that is shed, be [openly knowen] amongst the Heathen in our sight
Let the sorowfull sighing of the prisoners come before thee, accordyng vnto the greatnes of thy power: preserue thou those that [are] appoynted to dye
And rewarde thou our neighbours seuen folde into their bosome: their blasphemie wherewith they haue blasphemed thee O God
So we who be thy people and sheepe of thy pasture wyll confesse thee for euer: and we wyll alway set foorth in wordes thy prayse, from generation to generation
Heare O thou shephearde of Israel, thou that leadest Ioseph lyke a sheepe: and thou that sittest vpon the Cherubims, shew thy gratious presence
Before Ephraim, Beniamin, and Manasses: stirre vp thy strength, and come for to saue vs
Turne vs agayne O Lorde: shewe the light of thy countenaunce, and we shalbe saued
O God, Lorde of hoastes: howe long wylt thou be angry at the prayer of thy people
Thou feedest them with the bread of teares: and geuest them plenteously teares to drinke
Thou hast made vs a strife vnto our neighbours: and our enemies laugh vs to scorne
Turne vs agayne thou Lorde of hoastes: shewe the light of thy countenaunce, and we shalbe saued
Thou dydst translate a vine out of Egypt: thou didst cast out the Heathen, and planted it
Thou madst roome before it: thou causedst it to take roote, and it hath filled the lande
The hilles were couered with her shadowe: and goodly high Cedar trees with her bowes
She stretched out her braunches vnto the sea: and her bowes vnto the riuer
Why hast thou then broken downe her hedge: that all they whiche go by plucke of her grapes
The wylde bore out of the wood rooteth it vp: and the wylde beast of the fielde deuoureth it
(80: 14a) Turne thee agayne thou God of hoastes I pray thee: loke downe from heauen, beholde and visite this vin
(80: 14b) and vineyarde that thy ryght hande hath planted, and the young braunche which thou hast fortified for thy selfe
(80: 15) It is brent with fire and cut downe: they shall perishe at the rebuke of thy countenaunce
(80: 16) Let thy hande be vpon the man of thy right hande: and vpon the sonne of man whom thou hast fortified for thyne owne selfe
(80: 17) And so we wyll not go backe from thee: thou shalt reuiue vs, and we wyll call vpon thy name
(80: 18) Turne vs agayne O God, Lorde of hoastes: shewe the light of thy countenaunce, and we shalbe saued
Sing we meryly vnto the Lorde our strength: make a chearefull noyse vnto the Lorde of Iacob
Take the psalterie: bryng hyther the tabret, the merie harpe, with the lute
Blowe vp the trumpet in the newe moone, euen in the time appointed: and vpon our solempne feast day
For this was made a statute for Israel: and a lawe of the God of Iacob
This he ordayned in Ioseph for a testimonie, when he came out of the lande of Egypt: [where] I hearde a tongue [whiche] I knewe not
I eased his shoulder from the burthen: and his handes ceassed from making pottes
Thou calledst vpon me in troubles, and I deliuered thee: I hearde thee out of the middest of a thunder, I proued thee also at the waters of strife. Selah
[ Then I sayd] heare O my people: and I wyll geue thee a charge O Israel in protesting vnto thee
If thou wylt hearken vnto me, there shall be no straunge God in thee: neither shalt thou geue worship to any other Lorde beside me
I am God thy Lorde which brought thee out of the land of Egypt: open thy mouth wyde, and I wyll fill it
But my people woulde not heare my voyce: and Israel would not [obey] me
So I gaue them vp vnto the wicked cogitations of their owne heartes: and I did let them folowe their owne imaginations
O that my people woulde haue hearkened vnto me: O that Israel had walked in my wayes
I should soone haue tamed their enemies: and turned myne hande against their aduersaries
The haters of God shoulde haue ben founde liers: and their time should haue endured for euer
He woulde haue fed them also with the finest wheate flowre: and I would haue satisfied thee with honie out of the stonie rocke
God standeth in the congregation of God: he iudgeth in the midst of God
Howe long wyll ye geue wrong iudgement: and accept the persons of the vngodly? Selah
Iudge ryght vnto the poore and fatherlesse: dispatch according to iustice suche as be afflicted and in necessitie
Deliuer the poore and outcast: saue them from the hande of the vngodly
They knowe nothyng, they vnderstande nothing: they walke on styll in darknesse, [wherfore] all the foundations of the earth be out of course
I haue sayde ye are gods: and ye all are chyldren of the most highest
But ye shall dye lyke as a man [doth:] and princes them selues shall fall away lyke as other [do.
Arise O God, and iudge thou the earth: for thou shalt take all Heathen to thine inheritaunce
Holde not thy tongue O Lorde: kepe not styll scilence, refraine not thy selfe O Lorde
For beholde, thyne enemies make an vprore: and they that hate thee, haue lifted vp their head
They haue deuised shrewde counsell against thy people: and they haue consulted against thyne, whom thou defendest
They haue said, come, and let vs roote them out, that they be no more a people: and that the name of Israel may be no more in remembraunce
For they haue conspired all in one minde: & are confederate against thee
The pauilions of Edom and the Ismaelites: of Moab, and Hagerites
Gebal, and Ammon, and Amalec: the Philistines with the inhabitauntes of Tyre
Assur also is ioyned vnto them: they were a great ayde to the chyldren of Lot. Selah
But do thou vnto them, as vnto Midian: as vnto Sisera, as vnto Iabin at the brooke Kishon
Whiche perished at Ein Dor: and became as the doung of the earth
Make them, their princes, [and] al their captaynes: lyke Oreb, and lyke Zeeb, and lyke Salmunna
Whiche sayd, let vs take to our selues: the houses of God in possession
O my Lorde, make them lyke vnto a wheele: and as chaffe before the winde
Lyke as a fire that burneth vp the wood: and as the flambe that consumeth the mountaynes
Persecute them euen so with thy tempest: and make them afrayde with thy storme
Make shame to appeare in their faces: that they may seeke thy name O God
Let them be confounded and astonied with feare euer more & more: let them be put to shame, and perishe
And let them knowe that thou in thy name God eternall art only: O thou the most highest ouer all the earth
O how amiable are thy dwellinges: thou God of hoastes
My soule hath a desire and a longing to enter into the courtes of God: my heart and my flesh leapeth with ioy for to go to the liuing Lorde
Yea the sparowe hath founde her an house, and the swallowe a nest: where she may lay her young: euen thy aulters O God of hoastes, my king & my Lord
Blessed are they that dwell in thy house: they wyll be alway praysyng thee. Selah
Blessed is that man whose strength is in thee: [thy] wayes are in their heart
They iourneying through the vale of teares: (yea when euery cesterne [at their name] is filled with water) do accept it for a [fayre pleasaunt] well
They wyl set forward from a stoute courage to a stoute courage: that the God of Gods may be seene of them in Sion
O God Lorde of hoastes heare my prayer: geue eare O God of Iacob. Selah
Beholde O Lorde our shielde: and loke vpon the face of thyne annointed
For one day in thy courtes, is better then a thousande [els where ]: I had rather be a doore keper in the house of my God, then to dwell in [large] tabernacles of vngodlynes
For God the Lorde is a sunne and a shielde: God geueth grace and worship, he withholdeth no good thyng from them that liue in any perfection
O God of hoastes: blessed is the man that putteth his trust in thee
O God, thou art become gracious vnto thy land: thou hast brought Iacob agayne home out of captiuitie
Thou hast forgeuen the wickednes of thy people: and couered all their sinnes. Selah
Thou hast taken away al thy displeasure: and turned thy selfe from thy wrathfull indignation
Turne vs O God of our saluation: and let thyne anger ceasse from vs
Wilt thou be displeased at vs for euer? and wylt thou stretche out thy wrath from one generation to another
Wylt thou not turne agayne and reuiue vs: that thy people may reioyce in thee
Shew vs thy louing kindnes O God: and graunt vs thy saluation
I wyll hearken what God the Lord saith: for he speaketh peace vnto his people & to his saintes, that they turne not agayne to folly
For truely his saluation is nye them that feare him: insomuch that glory dwelleth in our earth
Mercy and trueth are met together: righteousnes and peace haue kissed [eche other.
Trueth shall bud out of the earth: and ryghteousnes shall looke downe from heauen
Yea, God shall geue all that is good: and our earth shall geue her encrease
[ Euery man] shall cause righteousnes to go before him: and he shall direct his steppes in the way
Bow downe thine eare O God, and heare me: for I am poore and in miserie
Preserue thou my soule, for I am holy: my God saue thy seruaunt that putteth his trust in thee
Be mercifull vnto me O God: for I do call dayly vpon thee
Comfort the soule of thy seruaunt: for vnto thee O Lord do I lift vp my soule
For thou Lorde art good and gracious: and of great mercy vnto all them that call vpon thee
Geue eare O God vnto my prayer: and be attentiue vnto the voyce of my humble petitions
I call vpon thee in the day of my trouble: for thou hearest me
Among the gods there is none like vnto thee O Lorde: there is not one that can do as thou doest
All nations whom thou hast made, shall come and worship thee O Lorde: and shall glorifie thy name
For thou art great and doest wonderous thinges: thou art God alone
Teache me thy way O God, and I wyll walke in thy trueth: make my heart all one with thyne, that it may feare thy name
I wyll acknowledge thee O Lorde my God with all my heart: and I wyl glorifie thy name for euer
For great is thy mercy towarde me: and thou hast deliuered my soule from the lowest [part of] hell
O God, the proude are rysen against me: a companie of outragious naughtipackes haue sought after my soule, and haue not set thee before their eyes
But thou O Lorde art a God full of compassion and mercy: long yet thou be angry, plenteous in goodnes and trueth
Turne thy face vnto me, and haue mercy vpon me: geue thy strength vnto thy seruaunt, and helpe the sonne of thine handmayde
Shewe some good token of thy fauour towardes me, that they whiche hate me may see it and be ashamed: because thou God hast helped me, and comforted me
(87: 1b) [for] her foundations are vpon the holy hilles
(87: 1a) God loueth the gates of Sion more then all the dwellynges of Iacob
(87: 2) Uery excellent thinges are spoken of thee: O thou citie of God. Selah
(87: 3) I wyll make mention amongst those that knowe me, of Egypt and Babylon: behold also of Palestina and Tyre, with Ethiopia, [and it shalbe sayde] suche a man is borne there
(87: 4) But of Sion it shalbe reported, that very many be borne in her: and the most highest him selfe shall establishe her
(87: 5) God wyll number in the register of the people: euery one that is borne there. Selah
(87: 6) And the singers aswell as the players of instrumentes: yea al my fountaines are in thee
(88: 1a) O God the Lorde of my saluation, I crye day and night before thee
(88: 1b) let my prayer enter into thy presence, encline thyne eare vnto my crying
(88: 2) For my soule is full of miserie: and my life toucheth the graue
(88: 3) I am counted as one of them that go downe vnto the pit: and I am nowe become a man that hath no strength
(88: 4) I am free among the dead: like such as beyng kylled lye in a graue, whom thou remembrest no more, and are cut away from thy hande
(88: 5) Thou hast layde me in the lowest pit: in darknes and in deepenes
(88: 6) Thyne indignation sore presseth me: and thou hast vexed me with all thy stormes. Selah
(88: 7) Thou hast put away myne acquaintaunce farre from me, and made me to be abhorred of them: I am shut vp, I can not get foorth
(88: 8) My sight fayleth through my affliction O God: I haue called dayly vpon thee, I haue stretched out mine handes vnto thee
(88: 9) Wylt thou worke a miracle amongst the dead? or shal the dead rise vp againe [and] acknowledge thee? Selah
(88: 10) Shall thy louing kindnes be talked of in the graue? or thy faythfulnes in destruction
(88: 11) Shall thy wonderous workes be knowen in the darke? and thy righteousnes in the lande of forgetfulnes
(88: 12) But vnto thee do I crye O God: and my prayer commeth early in the morning before thee
(88: 13) O God, why abhorrest thou my soule: and [why] hidest thou thy face from me
(88: 14) I am in miserie, I labour euen from my youth with the panges of death: I haue suffered thy terrours, [and] I am styll in doubt
(88: 15) Thyne indignation hath gone ouer me: and thy terrours haue vndone me
(88: 16) They came rounde about me dayly lyke water: and compassed me altogether on euery syde
(88: 17) Thou hast put a way farre from me my frende and neighbour: [thou hast hid] mine acquaintaunce out of sight
I wyll sing alwayes of the mercy of God: with my mouth I wyll make knowen thy trueth from one generation to another
For I sayde, mercy shall for euer endure: thou hast established thy trueth in the heauens
I haue made a couenaunt with my chosen: I haue sworne vnto Dauid my seruaunt
I wyll establishe thy seede for euer: and buylde vp thy throne from generation to generation. Selah
O God, the very heauens shall confesse thy wonderous workes: and thy trueth in the congregation of saintes
For who is he in the cloudes that shal matche God: [and who] is like vnto God amongst the children gods
God is very terrible in the assemblie of saintes: and to be feared aboue al them that are about him
O God, Lorde of hoastes, who is like vnto thee a most mightie Lorde: and thy trueth is on euery side thee
Thou rulest the ragyng of the sea: when her waues aryse, thou delayest them
Thou hast brought Egypt in so bad a case as if it were wounded: thou hast scattered thyne enemies abrode with thy mightie arme
The heauens are thine, the earth also is thine: thou hast layde the foundation of the rounde worlde, and of all the plentie that is therin
Thou hast made the north and the south: Tabor and Hermon do reioyce in thy name
Thou hast a mightie arme: thy hand is strong, and thy right hand is exalted
Iustice and iudgement is the foundation of thy throne: mercy and trueth shall go before thy face
Blessed is the people that knoweth a triumphant noyse: O God, they shall walke in the light of thy countenaunce
They shall make them selues merie dayly in thy name: and in thy righteousnes they shall exalt them selues
For thou art the glory of their strength: and in thy louing kindnes thou wylt lift vp our hornes
For our shielde is of God: and our king is of the most holy of Israel
Thou hast spoken somtimes in visions vnto thy saintes: and hast sayde, I haue added ayde vpon the mightie, I haue exalted one chose out of the people
I haue founde Dauid my seruaunt: I haue annoynted him with myne holye oyle
Therfore my hande shalbe assured vnto him: and mine arme shall strengthen hym
The enemie shal not be able to do him violence: the sonne of wickednesse shall not afflict hym
I wyll breake into peeces his foes before his face: and ouerthrowe them that hate hym
My trueth also and my mercy shalbe with hym: and in my name shall his horne be exalted
I wyll set also his dominion in the sea: and his right hande in the fluddes
He shall make inuocation vnto me: [saying] thou art my father O my God, and my fortresse of saluation
And I will make him my first borne: in higher state then kinges of the earth
My mercy wyll I kepe for hym euermore: and my couenaunt shal stand fast with hym
His seede also wyll I make to endure for euer: and his throne as the dayes of heauen
(89: 30a) But if his chyldren forsake my lawe, and walke not in my iudgement
(89: 30b) if they breake my statutes, and kepe not my commaundementes
(89: 31) I will then visite their transgressions with a rodde: and their wickednesse with stripes
(89: 32) Neuerthelesse, my louyng kyndnesse I wyll not take vtterly from hym: I wyl not breake my promise with hym
(89: 33) I wyll not violate my couenaunt: nor alter the thyng that is gone out of my lyppes
(89: 34) I haue sworne once by my holynesse: that I wyll not speake an vntrueth vnto Dauid
(89: 35) His seede shall endure for euer: and his throne shalbe as the sunne before me
(89: 36) [And] as the moone which shall continue for euermore: and shalbe a faithful witnesse in heauen. Selah
(89: 37) But thou hast abhorred & forsake thine annoynted: & art sore displeased at him
(89: 38) Thou hast broken the couenaunt of thy seruaunt: thou hast disgraced his crowne, [castyng it] on the grounde
(89: 39) Thou hast ouerthrowe all his walles: and broken downe his strong holdes
(89: 40) All they that go by the way spoyle hym: he is become a rebuke vnto his neyghbours
(89: 41) Thou hast exalted the ryght hande of his enemies: and made all his aduersaries to reioyce
(89: 42) Thou hast turned the harde edge of his sworde: and thou hast not lifted him vp in the battayle
(89: 43) Thou hast brought his noble estate to an ende: and hast cast his throne downe to the grounde
(89: 44) Thou hast shortened the dayes of his youth: and thou hast couered him with shame. Selah
(89: 45) O God howe long wylt thou hyde thy selfe? for euer? shall thy wrath burne lyke fire
(89: 46) Remember what I am, howe short my tyme is of lyfe: wherfore hast thou created in vayne all the sonnes of men
(89: 47) What man is he that lyueth and shall not see death? can he delyuer his owne soule from the hande of hell? Selah
(89: 48) Lorde where are become thy former olde louyng kyndnesses: [which] thou dydst sweare vnto Dauid by thy fayth [that thou wouldest perfourme.
(89: 49) Remember O Lorde the dishonour of thy seruauntes: I beare in my bosome [the dishonour of] all people that be mightie
(89: 50) Who beyng thine enemies O God do dishonour: who do dishonour the footsteppes of thine annoynted
(89: 51) Blessed be God for euermore: so be it, and so be it
Lorde thou hast ben our habitation: from one generation to another generation
Before the moutaynes were brought foorth, or euer the earth & the worlde were made: thou art God both from euerlastyng, and also vntyll euerlastyng
Thou turnest man most miserable euen vnto dust: thou sayest also, O ye children of men returne you into dust
For a thousande yeres in thy syght are but as yestarday that is past: and as a watch in the nyght
Thou makest them to flowe away, they are a sleepe: they be in the morning as an hearbe that groweth
In the mornyng it florisheth and groweth vp: in the euenyng it is cut downe and wythered
For we be consumed through thy displeasure: and we are astonyed through thy wrathfull indignation
Thou hast set our misdeedes before thee: and our sinnes wherof we be not priuie, in the lyght of thy countenaunce
For all our dayes do passe in thine anger: we spende our yeres as [in speaking] a worde

The dayes of our yeres be in all threescore yeres and tenne, and yf through strength [of nature] men come to foure score yeres: yet is their iolitie but labour and care, yea moreouer it passeth in haste from vs, and we flee from it
Who regardeth the force of thy wrath? for euen there after as a man feareth thee, so [feeleth he] thy displeasure
Make vs to knowe so our dayes, that we number them: and we wyll frame a heart [vnto] wisdome
Turne agayne O God (what, for euer [wylt thou be angry?]) and be gratious vnto thy seruauntes
Replenishe vs early in the mornyng with thy mercie: and we wyll crye out for ioy, and be glad all the dayes of our lyfe
Make vs mery accordyng to the dayes that thou hast afflicted vs: and accordyng to the yeres wherin we haue suffred aduersitie
Let thy worke appeare in thy seruauntes: and thy glory in their children
And let the glorious maiestie of the Lorde our God be vpon vs: and prosper thou the worke of our handes vpon vs, O prosper thou our handy worke
Whosoeuer sitteth vnder the couer of the most highest: he shal abide vnder the shadowe of the almightie
I wyll say vnto God, thou art my hope and my fortresse: my Lorde, in whom I wyll trust
For he wyll delyuer thee from the snare of the hunter: and from the noysome pestilence
He wyll couer thee vnder his wynges, & thou shalt be safe vnder his fethers: his faythfulnesse shalbe thy shielde and buckler
Thou shalt not be afrayde of any terrour of the nyght: nor of any arrowe that sleeth by day
Nor of any pestilence that walketh in the darknesse: nor of any deadly fyt that destroyeth at hygh noone
A thousande shall fall beside thee, and ten thousande at thy ryght hande: but it shall not come nygh thee
Thou only with thine eyes shalt beholde: & see the rewarde of the vngodly
For thou O God art my hope: thou hast set thine habitation very hygh
There shall no euyll lyght on thee: neither shall any plague come nye thy dwellyng
For he wyll geue his angels charge ouer thee: to kepe thee in all thy wayes
They wyll beare thee in [their] handes: that thou hurt not thy foote agaynst a stone
Thou shalt set thy foote vppon the Lion and Adder: the young Lion and the Dragon thou shalt treade vnder thy feete
Because he hath set greatly his loue vpon me, therfore wyll I deliuer hym: I wyll set hym vp out of all daunger, because he hath knowen my name
He shall call vpon me, and I wyll heare hym: yea I am with hym in trouble, I wyll deliuer hym, and bryng hym to honour
I wyll satisfie hym with a long lyfe: and I wyll cause hym to see my saluation
It is a good thyng to confesse vnto God: and to syng psalmes vnto thy name O thou most hyghest
To set foorth in wordes thy louyng kyndnesse early in the mornyng: and thy trueth in the nyght season
Upon an instrument of ten strynges, and vpon the Lute: vpon the Harpe with a solemne sounde
For thou God hast made me glad thorowe thy workes: I do reioyce in the workes of thy handes
O God howe glorious are thy workes? thy thoughtes are very depe
An vnwise man doth not consider this: and a foole doth not vnderstande it
Wheras the vngodly do bud vp greene as the grasse, and wheras all workers of iniquitie do florishe: that they [notwithstandyng] shalbe destroyed for euer and euer
But thou O God: art the most highest for euermore
For lo, thine enemies O God, lo thine enemies shall perishe: & all the workers of wickednesse shalbe destroyed
But my horne shalbe exalted lyke the horne of an vnicorne: for I am annoynted with excellent oyle
And myne eye shall see those that lye in wayte for me: myne eare shall heare the malitious persons that rise vp agaynst me
The ryghteous shall florishe lyke a paulme tree: and shall spread abroade like a Cedar in Libanus
Such as be planted in the house of God: shall florishe in the courtes of our Lorde
They shall styll bryng foorth fruite in their age: they shalbe fat and florishyng
For to set foorth in wordes that God is vpright: he is my rocke, and no iniquitie is in hym
God raigneth, he is clothed with a glorious maiestie, God is clothed with strength: he hath girded hym selfe, he hath made the worlde so sure that it can not be moued
Euer since the [worlde] began, thy throne hath ben set sure: thou art from euerlastyng
The fluddes are risen O God, the fluddes haue lyft vp their noyse: the fluddes haue lyft vp their waues
God which is on high, is more puissaut then the noyse of many waters: then the mightie waues of the sea
Thy testimonies are most certayne: holynesse is an ornament to thine house O God in all tymes
O God the Lord of [all] auengeaunce: the Lorde of [all] auengeaunce shewe thy [glorious maiestie.
Be exalted O thou iudge of the world: and rewarde the proude after their deseruyng
O God howe long shall the vngodly: howe long shall the vngodly triumph
All such as be workers of iniquitie: they babble, they prate shoutly, they make boastes of them selues
They oppresse thy people O God: and they afflict thine heritage
They murther the wyddowe and the straunger: & put the fatherlesse to death
And they say, tushe the Lorde seeth it not: neither doth the God of Iacob vnderstande it
Understande ye vnwyse among the people: O ye fooles, when wyll ye be well aduised
He that hath planted the eare, shall he not heare? yf he shapeth the eye, shall he not see
He that chasteneth the heathen, shall not he punishe? it is he that teacheth man knowledge
God knoweth the thoughtes of man: that they are but vanitie
Blessed is the man O Lorde, whom thou wylt chasten: and whom thou wylt instruct in thy lawe
That thou mayest geue hym patience in tyme of aduersitie: vntyll the pyt be digged vp for the vngodly
For God wyll not reiect his people: neither wil he forsake his inheritaunce
For iudgement shalbe reduced vnto iustice: and after it shall all such as be vpryght of heart [be iudged.
Who will ryse vp with me agaynst the malicious? or who wyll take my part agaynst workers of wickednesse
If God had not ben an ayde vnto me: it had not fayled much but my soule had dwelled in silence
But when I sayde my foote hath slypped: thy mercy O God helde me vp
In the multitude of my cogitations from the bottome of my heart: thy comfortes dyd recreate my soule
Shall the seate of wickednesse haue any thyng to do with thee: which [seate] maketh wrong to be enacted for a law
They flocke together agaynst the soule of the ryghteous: and condemne the innocent blood
But God is to me a refuge: and my Lorde is the rocke of my confidence
And he wyll recompence them their wickednesse, and destroy them in their owne malice: God our Lorde wyll destroy them
Come let vs syng vnto God: let vs make an heartie reioysyng with a loude voyce vnto the rocke of our saluation
Let vs make speede to come before his face with a confession: let vs expresse vnto hym outwardly a heartie gladnesse with syngyng of psalmes
For God is a great Lorde: and a great kyng aboue all gods
In his hande are all the deepe corners of the earth: and the hygh toppes of hylles be his also
The sea is his, and he made it: and his handes fashioned the drye lande
Come, let vs worshyp and fall downe: let vs kneele before the face of God our maker
For he is our Lorde: and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheepe of his hande
To day yf ye wyll heare his voyce harden not your heartes as in the tyme of contention: as in the day of temptation in the wildernesse
When your fathers tempted me, proued me: [yea after] they had seene my worke
Fourtie yeres long was I greeued with that generation: and I sayde this people erreth in heart, and they haue not knowen my wayes
Unto whom I sware in my wrath: that they shoulde not enter at all into my rest
Syng you vnto God a newe song: sing ye vnto God all [that be in] the earth
Syng ye vnto God and blesse his name: set foorth in wordes from day to day his saluation
Declare his glory amongst the heathen: and his wonderous actes amongst all the people
For God is great and worthy of all prayse: he is more to be feared then all gods
As for all the gods of the heathen they be but idoles: and it is God that made the heauens
Honour and maiestie be before hym: power and excellentnesse be in his sanctuarie
Geue vnto God O ye families of the people: geue vnto God glorie & power
Geue vnto God glorie [due] vnto his name: bryng an offeryng, and come into his courtes
Worshyp you God in the maiestie of holynesse: be you in dread of his face all [that be in] the earth
Set it foorth in wordes among the heathen that God raigneth: and that the worlde is set of a sure foundation, it shall not be remoued, he wyll iudge the people accordyng to equitie
The heauens shall reioyce, and the earth be glad: the sea shall make a noyse and all that is therin
The fielde shalbe ioyfull and all that is in it: then shall all the trees of the wood reioyce before the face of God
For he commeth, for he commeth to iudge the earth: he will iudge the world accordyng to iustice, and the people accordyng to his trueth
God raigneth, the earth shalbe glad: the multitude of the Iles shalbe glad [therof.
Cloudes and thicke darknesse are rounde about hym: iustice and iudgement are the habitation of his throne
There goeth a fire before his face: and burneth his enemies on euery syde
His lightninges gaue a lyght vnto the worlde: the earth sawe it and trembled
The hylles melted lyke waxe at the presence of God: at the presence of the Lorde of the whole earth
The heauens haue declared his iustice: and all the people haue seene his glorie
Confounded be all they that do seruice vnto carued images: and that do glorie in idols, but O gods, you all shall worshyp hym
Sion hearde of it, and reioyced: and the daughters of Iuda be glad, because of thy iudgementes O God
For thou art a God hygher then all [that are in] the earth: thou art exalted farre aboue all gods
You that loue God, hate the thyng which is euyll: he preserueth the soules of his saintes, he wyll delyuer them from the hande of the vngodly
There is sowen a lyght for the ryghteous: and gladnesse for such as be vpryght of heart
Reioyce in God O ye ryghteous: and prayse [hym] at the remembraunce of his holynesse
Syng vnto God a newe song: for he hath done marueylous thynges. (98: 2) With his owne right hande and with his holy arme: he hath gotten to hym selfe the victorie
(98: 3) God hath declared his saluation: he hath openly shewed his iustice in the syght of the heathen
(98: 4) He hath remembred his mercie and trueth towarde the house of Israel: and all the endes of the worlde haue seene the saluation of our Lorde
(98: 5) Shewe your selues ioyfull vnto God all ye [in] the earth: make a ioly noyse, reioyce you chearfully, & syng psalmes
(98: 6) Syng psalmes vnto God [playing] vpon an harpe: vpon an harpe, and with the sounde of a psalterie
(98: 7) Shewe your selues ioyfull before the kyng eternall: with trumpettes and sounde of shawmes
(98: 8) Let the sea make a noyse, and that is within it: the rounde worlde, and they that dwell therin
(98: 9) Let the fluddes clappe their handes: and let the hylles be ioyfull altogether before the face of God
(98: 10) For he commeth to iudge the earth: he wyll iudge the worlde accordyng to iustice, & the people accordyng to equitie
God raigneth, the people be in a rage: he sitteth [betweene] the Cherubims, the earth quaketh
God is great in Sion: and high aboue all people
They shall prayse thy name great & dreadfull: [for] it is holy, and a kynges power [that] loueth iudgement
Thou hast ordeyned [all thynges] accordyng to equitie: thou hast caused iudgement and iustice to be in Iacob
Magnifie God our Lorde: and kneele downe before his footstoole, for it is holy
Moyses & Aaron among his priestes, and Samuel among such as call vpon his name: [these] called vpon God, and he hearde them
He spake vnto them out of the cloudy pyller: for they kept his testimonies, and the lawe [that] he gaue them
O God our Lord thou heardest them, O Lorde thou didst forbeare them: and thou tokest auengement for their owne inuentions
Magnifie God our Lorde, and kneele downe before his holy hyll: for God our Lorde is holy
(100: 1a) Be ye ioyfull in God all that be in the earth
(100: 1b) serue God with gladnesse, and come before his face with a ioyfull noyse
(100: 2) Be ye sure that God is the Lorde, it is he that hath made vs, and not we our selues: we are his people and the sheepe of his pasture
(100: 3) Go your way into his gates with thankesgeuyng, and into his courtes with prayse: be thankfull vnto hym [and] blesse his name
(100: 4) For God is gratious, his mercie is euerlastyng: and his trueth [endureth] from generation to generation
I will sing of mercie and iudgement: I wyll syng vnto thee O God psalmes
I wyll endeuour my selfe to be fully instructed in the way of perfectnesse: when thou wylt come vnto me, I wil go vp and downe in the middest of my house in the perfectnesse of my heart
I wyll neuer set before myne eyes any deuillishe thyng: I wyll detest to do the worke of transgressours, it shall take no holde of me
A frowarde heart shall depart from me: I wyll not once knowe [any] euyll
I will destroy him who priuily slaundereth his neighbour: I wyll not suffer hym who hath a proude loke and a great stomacke
Myne eyes shalbe vpon such in the lande as haue a true meanyng, that they may sit with me: he that leadeth a perfect lyfe shall minister vnto me
There shall no deceiptfull person haue any seate in my house: he that telleth lyes shall not tary long in my syght
I wyll euery mornyng destroy all the vngodly in the lande: that I may roote out from the citie of God all workers of wickednesse
Heare my prayer O God: and let my crying come in vnto thee
Hyde not thy face from me in the day of my distresse: encline thine eare vnto me, heare me spedyly in the day that I call
For my dayes are consumed away like smoke: and my bones are burnt vp as though they were a firebrande
My heart is smitten downe and wythered lyke grasse: because I did forget to eate my bread
Through the noyse of my gronyng: my bones wyll scase cleaue to my fleshe
(102: 6a) I am become lyke a Pellicane of the wildernesse, and like an Owle that is in the desert
(102: 6b) I watch, and am as it were a sparrowe that sitteth alone vpon the house toppe
(102: 7) Myne enemies reuile me all the day long: and they that are in a rage against me, make their oth by me
(102: 8a) For I haue eaten asshes as it were bread, and mingled my drynke with weepyng
(102: 8b) because of thine indignation and wrath: for thou hast set me vp, and cast me downe
(102: 9) My dayes fade away lyke a shadowe: and I am wythered lyke grasse
(102: 10) But thou O God endurest for euer: and thy remembraunce throughout all generations
(102: 11) Thou wylt aryse vp, thou wylt haue compassion vpon Sion: for it is tyme that thou haue mercie vpon her, for the tyme appoynted is come
(102: 12) For thy seruauntes be well affected towarde her stones: and it pitieth them to see her in the dust
(102: 13) And the heathen wyll feare thy name O God: and all the kynges of the earth thy glorious maiestie
(102: 14) For God wyll buylde vp Sion: to be seene in his glorious maiestie
(102: 15) He wyll regarde the prayer of the humble destitute of all helpe: and he wyll not dispise their prayer
(102: 16) This shalbe written for those that come after: and the people which shalbe borne, shall prayse the Lorde
(102: 17) For he hath loked downe from his high sanctuarie: out of heauen did God beholde the earth
(102: 18) That he might heare the mourninges of such as be in captiuitie: and delyuer the children of death
(102: 19) That they may declare the name of God in Sion: and his prayse at Hierusalem
(102: 20a) When people were gathered together, & kyngdomes to serue God
(102: 20b) he afflicted my strength in the way, he shortened my dayes
(102: 21) But I say, O my God take me not away in the middest of myne age: as for thy yeres, they endure throughout all generations
(102: 22) Thou hast before tyme layde the foundation of the earth: and the heauens are the worke of thy handes
(102: 23) They shall perishe, but thou wylt remayne styll: they all shall waxe olde as doth a garment, and as a vesture thou wylt chaunge them, and they shalbe chaunged
(102: 24a) But thou art, and thy yeres can not fayle
(102: 24b) the children of thy seruauntes shal dwell, and their seede shalbe maynteyned in thy syght
Blesse God O my soule: and all that is within me [prayse] his holy name
Blesse God O my soule: and forget not all his benefites
Who forgeueth all thy wickednesse: and healeth all thine infirmities
Who redeemeth thy lyfe from destruction: [and] crowneth thee with mercie and louyng kyndnesse
Who satisfieth thy mouth with good thynges: causyng thy youth lyke an Egles to be renued
God executeth iustice and iudgement: for all them that are oppressed with wrong
He made his wayes knowen vnto Moyses: his workes vnto the children of Israel
God is full of compassion and pitie: loth to be angry, and exceedyng great in mercie
He vseth not to continue in chydyng: neither reserueth he [his anger] for euer
He dealeth not with vs accordyng to our sinnes: nor rewardeth vs according to our wickednesse
For accordyng to the hyghnesse of heauen aboue the earth: his mercie preuayleth to them that feare hym
